title: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti
hook: Krishna sets out to make peace himself, carrying Draupadi's words with him, and in Hastinapura he turns down a royal feast
carry: out of love, or out of need
tomorrow: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti

segments.voice: Yesterday in the Udyoga: Sanjaya pleaded for peace, and Yudhishthira asked for just five villages. Your line was five villages, and let this end.

Krishna decides to go to Hastinapura himself: one more try for peace, in person. Before he leaves, each of the brothers gives him a message, and several of them lean toward peace. Then Draupadi comes to him. She takes her long dark hair in her hand, the hair Duhshasana dragged her by in the dice hall, and holds it up. When you speak of peace, she says, remember this. If my husbands won't fight, my old father will, and my sons will. Krishna promises her she'll see justice, and sets off.
screen: `KRISHNA GOES HIMSELF.` → `DRAUPADI HOLDS UP HER HAIR.` → `REMEMBER THIS.`

segments.voice: Hastinapura gets ready for him. Duryodhana has rest houses built along the road and lays out a great feast. This is diplomacy as hospitality: if Krishna eats at his table, he's half won. Krishna passes the rest houses by. In the city he greets the old king, then goes to Kunti, the Pandavas' mother, who has been living in Vidura's house all these years. She weeps and asks after her sons, one by one. Only then does Krishna go to Duryodhana's palace. He accepts his greeting, and declines the meal. Duryodhana is offended. Why won't you eat with us? Krishna's answer is short and sharp. A person eats another's food either out of love, or out of need. You feel no love for me, and I'm in no need. So he walks back to a much plainer house: the home of Vidura, the wise half-brother of the king, who spoke up for the Pandavas years ago in the dice hall. That's where Krishna eats, and where he stays. Look at what he does before he says a word in the assembly. Draupadi's hair goes with him. He won't eat at the table of a man who means harm. He sleeps under the roof of a man who told the truth when it was dangerous. He visits the mother first. An embassy isn't only speeches. It's where you eat, where you sleep, and whom you visit first.
screen: `DRAUPADI'S HAIR GOES WITH HIM` · `KUNTI ASKS AFTER HER SONS` · `A FEAST DECLINED` · then, large: `SUPPER AT VIDURA'S`

segments.voice: Krishna named two honest reasons to share a table, love or need; bring to mind someone who has fed you, in any sense, out of love. Breathing in, remember one meal or one kindness from them, and breathing out, let yourself be grateful, then think of someone you might feed, in any sense. If you pray, you can hold both of them in your prayer.
Udyoga. The getting ready, where Krishna carries Draupadi's words to Hastinapura and eats at Vidura's plain table.
Your line: out of love, or out of need. A feast turned down, and a plain supper at Vidura's. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Krishna's refusal of Duryodhana's feast and his meal at Vidura's house are retold in Hindu devotional storytelling, where Vidura's humble hospitality is remembered with affection.

fork.setup: you're Krishna, come to Hastinapura to talk peace. Duryodhana has laid out a grand feast in your honor. what do you do?
options: eat, and use the goodwill in tomorrow's talks.
decline: people share food out of love or need, and here there's neither.
eat a little and leave early.
fork.reveal: Krishna declines, says exactly that, and goes to eat at Vidura's plain house instead.

original.note: effort, getting ready; in this book Krishna's own journey to Hastinapura is part of the effort for peace.

trapdoor: what you thought: Krishna was just being rude to Duryodhana.
what it means: refusing the feast keeps him free; he won't accept hospitality meant to bind him.

chat.says: Why did Krishna refuse Duryodhana's feast and eat at Vidura's plain house instead?
options: One eats another's food out of love or need; Duryodhana felt no love, and Krishna had no need.
He wanted to insult Duryodhana in front of the court to start the war sooner.
He was fasting that day for the success of the peace talks in the assembly.
chat.meaning: Krishna says one eats another's food out of love or out of need. Duryodhana felt no love for him, and he was in no need.

Hastinapura.meaning: the Kuru capital, seat of Dhritarashtra's court

Kunti.meaning: the Pandavas' mother, living in Vidura's house

Vidura.meaning: the wise half-brother of King Dhritarashtra

Duhshasana.meaning: Duryodhana's brother, who dragged Draupadi by the hair

Draupadi.meaning: the Pandavas' queen, who sends her hair as a reminder

recall: daughter of King Bhima of Vidarbha
